item.title: Harnessing Technological Innovation for Managing Volatility and Advancing Sustainable and Regenerative Supply Chains
item.content:encoded:
Md Maruf Hossan Chowdhury, University of Technology Sydney

Shahriar Akter, University of Wollongong

Mohammad Alamgir Hossain, RMIT University

Kristijan Mirkovski, Deakin University

Supply chains face mounting pressures from climate change, geopolitical tensions, and pandemic risks, while stakeholders demand greater sustainability. Digital technologies like artificial intelligence and blockchain offer solutions for enhancing visibility and improving environmental and social outcomes.

The integration of digital innovation with sustainability and resilience strategies enables supply chains to reduce systemic risks while strengthening their ability to recover from disruptions. However, significant gaps remain in understanding how these technologies influence ESG performance and interact with contextual factors.

This special issue seeks high-quality contributions exploring how digital and emerging technologies enable or constrain sustainable, resilient, and regenerative supply chain strategies, offering theoretical insights and practical implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers.

  • Digital product passports and lifecycle data integration

  • Techno-nationalism and sovereign AI in global supply chains

item.title: Resilient, Inclusive and Digital Supply Chains for Africa's Sustainable Development
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how supply chains can advance sustainable development across Africa by integrating resilience, inclusivity, and digital innovation. The focus encompasses strategies to manage disruptions in volatile environments, approaches to include SMEs and local communities in value chains, and the application of artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies to enhance efficiency and transparency.

The issue welcomes rigorous, peer-reviewed contributions from academics, practitioners, and policymakers addressing digital transformation, risk management, sustainability, and sector-specific applications in healthcare and agribusiness. The goal is to develop equitable, robust supply chain systems that support Africa's sustainable development objectives.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Building resilient and risk-responsive supply chains

item.title: A systemic understanding of supply chain resilience: cross-level interactions, multi-level frameworks, and theoretical innovations
item.content:encoded:
Guoqing Zhao, Swansea University

Samuel Fosso Wamba, TBS Business School

Maciel M. Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Recent large-scale disruptions including pandemics, geopolitical conflicts, and climate disasters have revealed how disturbances cascade across supply chain levels, causing systemic failures. While supply chain resilience has become prominent in research, existing literature remains fragmented, typically examining single analytical levels without comprehensive systemic perspective.

This special issue advances systemic understanding of supply chain resilience by examining cross-level interactions and building multi-level frameworks. The issue seeks research treating resilience as a dynamic capability emerging from interactions across individual, organizational, supply chain, and environmental levels, exploring how factors at different levels influence each other, applying theoretical frameworks like systems theory and panarchy theory, investigating technology's mediating role, and developing practical tools for managers.

item.title: Essay Frontiers: A Call for Bold Ideas, New Voices, and New Directions in Logistics and SCM
item.content:encoded:
Maciel Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Morgane Fritz, Excelia Business School

Britta Gammelgaard, University of Southern Denmark

Logistics and supply chain management (L/SCM) have advanced through analytical rigor and empirical refinement. However, the contemporary landscape, shaped by geopolitical shifts, digital transformation, climate pressures, and evolving societal expectations, requires more than incremental extensions of existing models. It calls for a reconsideration of the assumptions, values, and conceptual boundaries that underpin the field. Many of the most pressing challenges in L/SCM today are not only empirical, but also normative, philosophical, and inherently interdisciplinary.

This special issue seeks essays that move beyond established paradigms and offer reflective, provocative, and conceptually grounded perspectives that offer new lenses and open new directions for research and practice. The objective is to complement empirical work by fostering ideas that challenge, reframe, and extend our understanding of L/SCM.
